claim: Sciaticyl is a capsule sold to support the sciatic nerve and relieve leg pain from sciatica. Its formula combines B vitamins and magnesium with antioxidants studied for nerve pain, such as alpha-lipoic acid and acetyl-L-carnitine.
ing_note: The label is described on the website, but amounts aren't given in text. The page lists 'N-Acetyl L-Carnitine', which appears to mean acetyl-L-carnitine.
price_note: A 3-bottle package is also offered with free US shipping; its total appears on the order page.
refund_note: Contact customer service within 90 days of purchase for a full refund.
made: Made in the US in a GMP-certified facility (seller's claim).
checks: Alpha-lipoic acid has the best evidence here, mainly for diabetic nerve pain at 600 mg a day; evidence for sciatica specifically is limited.
Acetyl-L-carnitine has small trials for neuropathy and one Italian study in sciatica-related pain.
B vitamins help nerve pain only if you are deficient (B12 deficiency is common in older adults and people on metformin).
Claims that it can 'eliminate the need' for chiropractic care or prescription medicine aren't supported.
pros: Ingredients with genuine nerve-pain research (ALA, ALC)
cons: Doses not stated in text, so ALA may be under the studied 600 mg
Sciatica usually improves with movement and time, making results hard to judge
verdict: Sciaticyl is one of the more sensible nerve formulas we've reviewed, because alpha-lipoic acid and acetyl-L-carnitine have real research behind them. Most sciatica settles within weeks with activity and physical therapy. See a doctor urgently if you have leg weakness, numbness in the groin area or bladder changes.
